title: The Penny Stall Michael Marks Ran Two Days a Week in Leeds
conflicts: Arrival year: the M&S timeline says he arrived in England in 1884, but the archive's exhibitions, MyLearning and the Migration Museum give 1882 with peddling 1882-1884; story uses 1882. Birth year uncertain (1859/1863/1864); story gives only 'about nineteen' on leaving in 1882. Covered-market move: archive and MyLearning say 1886, Knitting Together ties it to 1894; story uses 1886. Wikipedia calls the Dewhirst arrangement goods on terms rather than a loan; story follows the archive's £5 loan. Growth figures for 1900 differ between MoneyWeek and the archive and are not used.
notes: Marks left no first-hand account; the decision (better stock at higher cost, hoping for turnover, because he could not match neighbours' banter) is the account of M&S archivist Paul Bookbinder on the archive page and is attributed to the company's archivists. The repeat screen flagged a Maggie Lena Walker penny-bank edition as same-founder but let it through; it is a different person and company. Company field written 'Marks' Penny Bazaar (later Marks & Spencer)', the stall's own name in 1884.
